analysis.title: US Macro Weekly: Fed in the spotlight in a busier week
key_insights: The week holds the October FOMC meeting plus PCE inflation, the advance Q3 2026 GDP report and personal income and spending. The authors wrote on 16 October ahead of travel and reserve the right to change forecasts based on data released in the interim.

The October FOMC is a closer call after upside surprises in September CPI and PPI. CA-CIB still leans toward a skip in October followed by another hike in December. They say consecutive hikes would be the better approach, but their job is to project what the Fed will do.

NY Fed President Williams, Vice Chair Jefferson and Governor Waller have hinted at a preference to stay on hold in October. Waller said the Fed will likely need to hike more but has flexibility on timing, since hikes do not need to come at consecutive meetings. CA-CIB reads this group as biased toward holding, with the inflation data not quite reaching the bar to act.

September PCE is released the day after the Fed meeting. CA-CIB expects core PCE up about 0.33% MoM (rounding up to 0.4% cannot be ruled out) with YoY edging up to 3.1% from 3.0%, and headline PCE up 0.5% MoM with YoY at 3.6% from 3.4%. This keeps additional hikes, such as in December, on the table but may not reach the bar for the committee to hike in October.

CA-CIB expects personal income up 0.2% MoM and personal spending up 0.5% MoM. Real spending would be relatively soft given the PCE deflator, but follows a very strong August, and consumption is on track for another solid quarter in the 3% range.

CA-CIB expects Q3 2026 GDP to accelerate to 3.0% QoQ SAAR from 2.2% in Q2, driven by strong consumption and robust non-residential investment. This would show the economy has stayed resilient despite the ongoing war in Iran.

Headline durable goods orders are expected to rise strongly on a surge in Boeing orders, though the headline is noisy. Consumer confidence is likely weaker, which has not been a good signal for actual spending recently, and new home sales are expected on the softer side.

The Fed hiked in September. CA-CIB expects two more 25bp hikes in December and March, taking the upper bound back to 4.50% and reversing the late 2025 insurance cuts, with consecutive hikes a risk. They then project two 25bp cuts in Q4 2027 to bring the upper bound to 4.00%.

CA-CIB forecasts 2026 US GDP growth of 2.3% and 2027 growth of 2.1%. The 2026 figure was cut from 2.5% because of the Iran war. Supports include fiscal support from the Big, Beautiful Bill, a diminishing trade policy drag and AI-related investment. The K-shaped, concentrated nature of growth is a risk.

CA-CIB has headline CPI peaking at 4.2% YoY in May and staying above 3.0% into early 2027 before dropping to the low 2.0% range from Q2 2027. Core CPI is forecast to hover between about 2.4% and 2.7% through early 2027 and slow to around 2.3% by end-2027. The Iran war energy spike adds upside risk to inflation forecasts.

CA-CIB sees the unemployment rate peak at 4.5% in November 2025 and expects stabilisation in the low 4% range through year-end and 2027. AI replacing some job functions could act as a headwind and slow the decline.

geopolitical: The ongoing war in Iran is a drag on 2026 US growth and has caused an energy price spike that adds upside risk to inflation forecasts. The report says the US is less vulnerable than many others.
US 2026 midterm election updates are listed among CA-CIB's recent publications, with more seats shifting towards Democrats.

tension_points.bull_case: Hawkish case: upside surprises in September CPI and PPI, a firm September PCE and a resilient economy argue for acting in October. CA-CIB itself thinks consecutive hikes would be the better approach.
tension_points.bear_case: Dovish-on-timing case: Williams, Jefferson and Waller have hinted at staying on hold in October to gather more information. Waller said the Fed has flexibility on timing, so hikes need not come at consecutive meetings.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A core PCE print that rounds up to 0.4% MoM or other data that clears the bar for the broader committee, plus new signals from the Fed members who favor a hold, would shift the call toward an October hike.

theme_stances.key_argument: The group of Fed members leaning toward holding would need to be convinced to act in October, and the inflation data does not quite reach that bar.
theme_stances.evidence: we continue to lean towards a skip in October followed by another hike in December
